Prior Predictive Checks for a Joint Bernoulli Design

Source: R/profile_prior_predictive.R
profile_prior_predictive.Rd

Draws beta/eta from the declared priors (design$stan_data$beta_sd/eta_sd – i.e. whatever profile_build_design was actually called with, not a separately-specified prior), computes the implied joint-state distribution at each event's REAL covariates via the SAME prediction kernel the Stan model/profile_ppc/ profile_estimate use, and summarizes it by group: per-class resistance margins, selected pair probabilities, the two most extreme profiles (all-resistant, all-susceptible), the resistance-count distribution, and a concentration/entropy summary. This is a check on the PRIOR alone – it never looks at Y, and a prior that looks implausible here is a prior problem, not evidence the data disagrees with it.

Usage

profile_prior_predictive(
  design,
  ids,
  n_draws = 1000L,
  ci_level = 0.95,
  seed = 123L
)

Arguments

design

List from profile_build_design (reads $stan_data: X, B, V, beta_sd, eta_sd; and $design: class_names).

ids

Data frame, one row per event (matching nrow(X)), with a group column.

n_draws

Integer. Prior draws. Default 1000L (prior draws are cheap – no Stan sampling – so this can be large).

ci_level

Numeric. Default 0.95.

seed

Integer. Default 123L.

Value

A list of data frames, each one row per group (x the family's own extra key):

class_margins

group x class: mean, lower, upper prior-predictive resistance probability.

pair_probabilities

group x class-pair x cell (RR/RS/SR/SS): mean, lower, upper.

extreme_profiles

group: all_resistant_mean/ lower/upper, all_susceptible_mean/lower/upper, and independence_all_resistant/independence_all_susceptible – what the all-R/all-S probability WOULD be under independence at this group's OWN mean marginal rates (the product of class_margins), so a prior-induced value far above the independence baseline signals strong prior-induced association, not just "a small number".

count_distribution

group x count (0..D resistant classes): mean, lower, upper.

concentration

group: mean_entropy (mean, across events and draws, of the per-event Shannon entropy of the 2^D-state distribution, in nats), max_entropy (\(\log(2^D)\), the uniform-distribution ceiling), and entropy_ratio (mean_entropy / max_entropy – near 0 means near-deterministic profiles; near 1 means close to the uniform/no-information prior).

Details

Inspect whether the prior puts most of its mass on near-deterministic profiles (entropy near 0) or implausibly strong cross-class associations (e.g. all-resistant/all-susceptible probability far above what independence at the marginal rates would give) across most hospitals BEFORE fitting. When increasing D or the interaction order, re-run this: many individually modest coefficients can combine into an extreme combined score, so a prior that looked fine at a smaller D is not guaranteed to still look fine at a larger one – rescaling by a fixed formula without re-inspecting the induced distribution is exactly the mistake this function exists to catch.
